extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: An n-way parallel speech and text dataset in 102 languages built on the FLoRes-101 machine translation benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language and approximately 1.4 thousand hours overall. It contains natural human read speech, transcripts, and parallel text for evaluating multilingual speech representations.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages covering 17 language families and 27 unique writing systems; the full language list is provided in Table 9.
extraction.citeAs: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, and Ankur Bapna. FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech. arXiv:2205.12446v1 [cs.CL], 25 May 2022.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors used the 2009 sentences from the publicly available FLoRes-101 dev and devtest sets and divided them into new train, dev, and test sentence splits containing 1509, 150, and 350 sentences, respectively. For each sentence in each of 102 languages, three recordings were collected from three different native speakers, imposing a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible. Additional workers evaluated whether each recording corresponded to its input sentence, and invalid recordings were discarded. Collected speech was split into train, development, and test sets with a target ratio of 7:1:2 and disjoint speakers between train/dev and test.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first dataset version, about 21.5% of sentences are missing because none of their three recordings were validated. Each sentence has between zero and three retained recordings. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text originates from FLoRes-101, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators. FLEURS uses only the 2009 publicly available dev and devtest sentences, together with English, and newly collected readings by native speakers. Recordings include both quiet and noisy environments.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Recordings are retained as collected, without data augmentation such as SpecAugment, speed perturbation, or simulated reverberation. The authors rename FLoRes 'Chinese (Simp)' to 'Mandarin Chinese' with code 'cmn' and 'Chinese (Trad)' to 'Cantonese Chinese' with code 'yue'. Each sentence has an integer index between 1 and 2009 that identifies parallel sentences across languages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid recordings are discarded following human validation. Speech has a sampling rate of 16 kHz, and all segments are within 30 seconds. Text preprocessing applies NFC followed by FST normalization, lowercasing, normalization, and punctuation removal. Words are also split into characters with a word-boundary token. Three transcript versions are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC_RAW), the preprocessed transcript (SRC_NORM), and its character-based version (SRC_CHAR).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Source transcripts are reused from the human translations produced for FLoRes-101. English translated transcripts are also retained. After recording, additional workers evaluate whether each recording corresponds to the input sentence; invalid recordings are discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human validation determines whether a recording matches its input sentence. Rejected recordings are removed, leaving zero to three recordings per sentence. No recordings are retained for a sentence when all three fail validation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill the missing sentences in future dataset versions. No update schedule, maintainer assignments, or deprecation policies are specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collection process involves speakers' native language and sex, with a target sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible. Speaker distinctions are used to create disjoint dataset splits.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable speech technology in more languages, catalyze research in low-resource and few-shot speech understanding, and support progress toward speech technologies for everyone. The paper identifies reducing performance gaps across geographical language groups as an important future research direction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of read speech derived from Wikipedia sentences, with approximately 12 hours of supervision per language and segments no longer than 30 seconds. About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of their recordings passed validation. The authors warn that training a giant model from scratch on FLEURS will easily overfit.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, fine-tuning, development, testing, and evaluation of multilingual speech representations for automatic speech recognition, speech language identification, speech-to-text and speech-to-speech translation, and multilingual speech-to-speech, text-to-text, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech retrieval, including cross-lingual and zero-shot evaluation. The paper recommends the character-based SRC_CHAR transcripts for ASR and adopts pre-training followed by fine-tuning rather than training a giant model from scratch.
